established_findings: TWO_VIDEO_DEV_BENCHMARK=PASS for two independent source videos, two frozen queries, and four video-query tasks.
The R3 fixed 10-second temporal-NMS revision matrix has 72/72 valid cells, complete schedules and snapshots, with zero replay, future access, visibility violation, failure, or deadline miss.
Reference scoring finds FIFO is the best method in this matrix, with macro AnytimeAUC_F1 0.0450066276, macro F1 0.0541666667, and two mean-summed T_high unique events.
FIFO's advantage is confined to one V0_Q1 event selected by creation-order VERIFY; all methods are null on both V1 tasks.
important_failures_and_lessons: R3 changes some V1 VERIFY rankings but is endpoint-equivalent to score-only and creates no cross-video quality gain.
FIFO recovers V0_Q1 because the oldest candidate unit 173 is a reference-matched true positive; score-only and R3 choose higher-scored negative unit 86.
Candidate capacity does not bind in V0_Q1, so retention is not the cause of the FIFO/R3 difference.
V1 nulls are compatible with the conservative fixed schedule exposing no reference-positive units; this limits mechanism interpretation but does not rescue R3.
next_highest_value_action: Obtain a third independent source video, retain Q1/Q2, and run six-task generalization validation without opening held-out.
objective: Determine whether one frozen low-cost proxy and an exposure-aware candidate frontier produce directionally consistent physical PSVR gains across two independent source videos and two frozen queries.

rejected_hypotheses.reason: The original design and only allowed R3 revision fail the preregistered task-direction, substantive-threshold, and cross-video requirements.

unresolved_uncertainties: Whether a materially different core route generalizes on an independent third source video.
Whether FIFO's single-event V0 advantage survives any new source rather than reflecting a creation-order coincidence.
How much conservative tail-bound schedule planning, rather than frontier policy, contributes to V1 nulls.
